body_content:
Hello everybody,

 

Information from the client :

They want our color to match the « profiles » of the mats in the main entrance

Supplier : GEGGUS

Product range : TOP CLEAN TREND 22 C32 BRONZE CLAIR 080 SAND. 

Color of the profiles : C32 Bronze clair (light bronze)

 

https://www.geggus.fr/produits/tapis-d-entree/premium-structure-aluminium/top-clean-trend/top-clean-trend-22-reps

 

They should choose to have this color on the visible elements when the lift is in its normal home position, including the top 3 mm trims.

And also on the button post if they choose it and also the button stations on upper and lower landing.

 

 

Cordialement

 

YANN BERJONNEAU

06 85 56 37 28

Yeah, this seems to fit the bill. Ultimately we need to know what C32 is as a finish and need a reference sample, and what their expectations are on delivery. Then it's for Karol to tell me the size of the components so we can assess whether this finish is possible in the UK and whether the process of achieving that finish is achievable by the supplier that we have.

Cc: Karol Porwol <karolp@sesameaccess.com>; Purchasing - Sesame Access <purchasing@sesameaccess.com>
Subject: Re: Project 17 Haussmann - color

 

Hi Yann,

Sorry I missed your call yesterday.

Giles/Karol, please read this and let me know if I have missed anything.

Yes, I am confident we can achieve a light bronze appearance on the Kensington. The point we need to confirm is the precise match to C32 Steel Brushed Light Bronze, including the brushed texture and sheen, rather than just the colour.

I understand from your last email that you cannot obtain a physical sample and that the client wants us to supply one. We can work from that direction. Could you send me the manufacturer’s name, catalogue page or website link where they have selected C32? We can then identify the intended finish and arrange a sample from our side. If they only have the description, we can offer our closest light bronze option for their approval, without presenting it as an exact C32 match.

There are different ways of achieving these finishes. We can apply a chemical patina to stainless steel in our workshop, and we also have an electrical brush plating process. They are not the same thing. The patina can be a useful, economical way of making the small visible trim edges blend with the surrounding finishes, but the colour can vary, particularly over larger surfaces.

For a closely matched brushed bronze appearance across larger visible faces, I would have our specialist finisher assess the reference before choosing the process. We can also use different methods for the trims and button station faceplates where appropriate, with the samples considered together so the overall appearance works.

The options already shown in our quotation cover different amounts of metalwork:

£2,700 covers the specified visible elements when the lift is in its normal home position, including the top 3 mm trims. The additional parts revealed as the lift rises remain stainless steel.

£8,500 covers the full stainless steel finishing scope described in the quotation, including the parts exposed when the lift rises.

The button station faceplate finishing is listed separately at £250.

These are the quoted options, rather than confirmation that the exact C32 finish has already been matched. Once we have identified the reference and agreed the component scope, we can confirm the proposed method, whether any additional specialist work is needed, and the timing before proceeding.

Could you confirm whether the client wants the bronze finish only on the metalwork visible with the lift lowered, or also on everything revealed during operation? That is the main distinction between the two larger options.

We would then arrange a representative sample showing the proposed colour, brushing and any protective coating for the client to approve before the lift parts are finished.

Regards,

 

Steven Lyons
